question: True or false: in 1988, laser-cooled sodium atoms measured about five times colder than theory said lasers could reach?
answer: True. Theory set a floor, the Doppler limit, at 240 millionths of a kelvin for sodium, because each photon absorbed or emitted kicks the atom at random. A US team measured 43 and checked it several ways. The theory had pictured a simpler atom; real sodium was climbing hills of light, shedding energy at each top.
move: A proven limit is only as real as the model it was proved in.
trap: Taking a floor derived from theory as a floor set by nature.
source: Lett et al., Physical Review Letters, 1988
